body:
PCCP Co-Founder and Senior Managing Partner William Lindsay (Photo credit: PCCP)

PCCP has disclosed $5 billion in combined fundraising for its latest real estate equity and credit funds, months after the two vehicles completed their final closes.

PCCP Equity X closed with $2.7 billion in January, up 50% from the $1.8 billion raised for its predecessor, while PCCP Credit XI reached a $2.3 billion final close in June, compared with $1.7 billion for the prior fund. Both vehicles exceeded their hard caps and are the largest PCCP has raised for their respective strategies.

The funds target U.S. middle-market investments across residential rental, industrial, retail and office properties. Equity X pursues opportunistic equity investments, while Credit XI focuses on value-add real estate credit.

“What resonated with investors is the fact that we have both a credit business and an equity business, and we have one investment team and one investment committee that services both,” Co-Founder and Senior Managing Partner William Lindsay said. “They’re very synergistic, so we believe we see a lot more deal flow than most.”

The Teacher Retirement System of Texas committed $200 million to Equity X. California State Teachers’ Retirement System committed $50 million to the equity fund and a total of $250 million to Credit XI, bringing disclosed commitments from the two pension systems to $500 million across the vehicles.

PCCP has already put a portion of the capital to work. As of September, the Los Angeles-based firm had executed about half of Equity X’s capital and allocated more than one-third of Credit XI.

Recent transactions have spanned both acquisitions and development. PCCP partnered with Stonemont to acquire a 38-building industrial portfolio for about $1 billion. The 5.9 million-square-foot portfolio spans Austin, Central Florida, Charlotte, Dallas and Phoenix and was 95% leased at the time of the transaction.

The firm also partnered with Guardian to acquire Ladd Tower, a 23-story, 332-unit apartment property in Portland, Oregon, for $63 million.

In the build-to-rent sector, PCCP entered an agreement with Integrity Community Builders to develop communities across multiple U.S. markets. PCCP agreed to provide up to $200 million of equity annually, with both firms co-investing in selected projects.

On the credit side, PCCP continues to focus on shorter-term, floating-rate bridge lending. “We expect new loan originations to remain active into 2027,” said Brian Heafey, co-manager of the firm’s debt platform.

PCCP manages about $30.1 billion as of June 30. Since its founding in 1998, the firm has managed, raised or invested more than $50.4 billion through funds, separate accounts and joint ventures.
